opening.argument: The video is presented as practical instruction on selling photographs through several established channels, including personal websites, stock services, physical prints, merchandise, and apps. It expressly teaches viewers “how to selling your photos online and start getting paid for your passion,” then explains that direct stock means “selling your photography on your own website.” The discussion of continuing revenue is qualified as merely having “the potential of making money for even years after you've posted it,” rather than promising a definite return. App competitions are further limited as “more of an entertainment exercise rather than a way to make consistent money.” Finally, viewers are told to read the terms and conditions before using stock sites, apps, or print-on-demand services, preserving attention to payment and ownership terms.

citations.quote: So in today's video, I'm going to teach you how to selling your photos online and start getting paid for your passion.
Direct stock is a term that refers to selling your photography on your own website.
The nice thing is that once you upload a photo for sale, it has the potential of making money for even years after you've posted it.
this is definitely more of an entertainment exercise rather than a way to make consistent money.
make sure that you're diligent in reading the terms and conditions before starting with any stock sites, apps, and print on demand services.
